issues.legal_issue: A decree-holder’s delivery request that describes resistance or obstruction is an application to have that obstruction adjudicated, even if it does not expressly identify the applicable procedural provision.
material_facts: A decree for possession was being executed, and the decree-holder sought a writ for delivery of possession.
The delivery request described a third party’s occupation and obstruction and sought removal of the obstruction.
issues.conclusion: The delivery request was in substance an application complaining of resistance or obstruction and had to be dealt with as such.
issues.legal_principle: Order XXI Rule 97 of the Code of Civil Procedure allows a decree-holder to apply when a person in possession resists or obstructs execution of a decree for possession. The nature and contents of the request, rather than whether it expressly names the rule, determine its character.

predicates.execution_of_possession_decree: A decree-holder sought to execute a decree requiring delivery of immovable property.
predicates.delivery_request_describes_obstruction: The decree-holder’s delivery request described resistance or obstruction by a person in possession and sought its removal.

issues.definition: When a decree-holder seeks delivery under a possession decree and the delivery request describes obstruction, the request is treated as an application complaining of obstruction.

issues.legal_issue: A third party claiming an independent right to possession may be heard before an order is made on a decree-holder’s application concerning obstruction to delivery of possession.
material_facts: A decree-holder sought delivery of property under an execution proceeding and described obstruction by the appellant.
The appellant claimed an independent right to the property and asserted that it was in possession.
The appellant had asked to be heard before an order was passed on the decree-holder’s request.
issues.conclusion: The appellant was entitled to be heard before the executing court passed an order on the decree-holder’s application.
issues.legal_principle: Order XXI Rule 97 applies where a decree-holder faces resistance or obstruction by any person in possession, including a person not bound by the decree. Shreemath and Anr. v. Rajesh and Ors., 1998 (4) SCC 543, supports the inclusion of such persons and the resolution of their claims at the execution stage.

predicates.execution_of_possession_decree: A decree-holder sought to execute a decree requiring delivery of immovable property.
predicates.decree_holder_alleges_obstruction: The decree-holder told the executing court that a person was obstructing delivery of the property.
predicates.third_party_claims_independent_possessio: A person other than the judgment debtor claimed an independent right to the property and asserted possession of it.

issues.definition: If a decree-holder alleges obstruction during execution and a third party claims an independent right and possession, the third party is entitled to be heard before the executing court orders further action.

issues.legal_issue: A third party’s separate suit concerning title and possession does not prevent the executing court from adjudicating relevant questions in the execution proceeding.
material_facts: The appellant claimed an independent right to the property and asserted possession.
The appellant had filed a separate suit seeking a declaration of title, confirmation of possession, and a declaration that the possession decree was not binding on it.
The appellant sought to be heard on the decree-holder’s obstruction application.
issues.conclusion: The separate suit did not justify refusing to hear the appellant in the execution proceeding; relevant questions had to be dealt with in that proceeding.
issues.legal_principle: Order XXI Rule 101 of the Code of Civil Procedure requires questions relating to title or interest that are relevant to an application under Rule 97 or Rule 99 to be determined by the court dealing with that application, rather than by a separate suit. The court relied on this provision in holding that the pending separate suit was not a reason to refuse a hearing in execution.

predicates.execution_of_possession_decree: A decree-holder sought to execute a decree requiring delivery of immovable property.
predicates.third_party_raises_relevant_title_or_int: A person other than the judgment debtor raised a claim to title or an interest in the property relevant to the execution dispute.
predicates.third_party_has_filed_separate_suit: The third party had also filed a separate suit concerning its claimed title or possession of the property.

issues.definition: When a third party raises a relevant title or interest claim in execution, filing a separate suit does not prevent the executing court from adjudicating that claim there.

issues.legal_issue: A third party resisting delivery of possession need not wait to be dispossessed before seeking adjudication of the obstruction in the execution proceeding.
material_facts: The appellant claimed an independent right to the property and asserted that it remained in possession.
The decree-holder sought delivery of possession despite the asserted obstruction.
The executing court treated an application after dispossession as the appellant’s only remedy.
issues.conclusion: The appellant was not required to wait for dispossession and then seek relief; the obstruction could be adjudicated before dispossession.
issues.legal_principle: Order XXI Rule 97 provides for adjudication when a decree-holder faces resistance or obstruction, while Rule 99 provides a remedy to a person other than the judgment debtor who has been dispossessed. Brahmdeo Chaudhary v. Rishikesh Prasad Jaiswal and Anr., 1997 (3) SCC 694, holds that an objector should not be required to surrender possession first and complain of dispossession later under Rule 99.

predicates.execution_of_possession_decree: A decree-holder sought to execute a decree requiring delivery of immovable property.
predicates.third_party_claims_independent_possessio: A person other than the judgment debtor claimed an independent right to the property and asserted possession of it.
predicates.delivery_is_being_resisted: The third party was resisting or obstructing delivery of the property before being dispossessed.

issues.definition: When a third party claims independent possession and resists delivery during execution, the third party need not wait for dispossession before seeking adjudication.
